role: ADR 004: explains why every quality rule is a numeric ceiling in .ci/*.txt that may only decrease, enforced by check_budget_monotonicity.sh.

units.does: no behavioural claim: ADR title 'Debt is ratcheted, never waived'.

units.key: § 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived > Context
units.does: Claims every quality rule (SwiftLint warnings, .shared uses, try? uses, ObservableObject conformances, fixed-point fonts, test skips, aggregate type size) has a numeric ceiling in .ci/*.txt. Verified: .ci/ holds swiftlint_warning_budget.txt (81), shared_usage_budget.txt (90), try_optional_budget.txt (170), legacy_observable_object_budget.txt (0), fixed_font_budget.txt (13), test_skip_budget.txt (9), aggregate_type_size_budget.txt (0).

flags.text: ADR says every quality rule is a numeric ceiling in .ci/*.txt 'rather than a pass/fail assertion', but the no-unowned gate and the strict-concurrency gate are hard pass/fail checks with no .ci budget file.

units.key: § 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived > Decision
units.does: Claims a ceiling may only move down: check_budget_monotonicity.sh fails on any increase lacking a 'budget-raise-ok:' trailer naming the file and reason; zero swiftlint:disable directives in Emuqu/Sources; refactor-spec gate counts justified exceptions separately. Verified: script header (check_budget_monotonicity.sh:14-29) implements the trailer and treats min_* files as floors; grep finds 0 swiftlint:disable in Emuqu/Sources; .ci/spec_justified_long_budget.txt (7) is separate from spec_long_functions_budget.txt (0).

flags.text: read_int accepts only integers and silently `continue`s past any other value, so the floor .ci/min_coverage_views.txt (43.5) is never compared: it can be lowered to any value without a budget-raise-ok trailer and the gate still prints 'clean'. The ADR's 'a ceiling may only move' guarantee does not hold for this file.

On a push to main, gates.yml compares the budgets only against HEAD~1, so in a multi-commit push a raise made in an earlier commit and left in place is invisible to the gate (it is already in HEAD~1). 'Fails the build on any increase' holds only per last commit.
ADR says the trailer must name 'the file and the reason'; the trailer parser extracts only the first token (the path) and accepts a trailer with no reason.

units.key: § 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived > Why not a hard zero
units.does: Argues against aspirational hard-zero gates, citing the old 90% coverage gate that could never pass. Current coverage floors are .ci/min_coverage.txt 44, min_coverage_logic.txt 45, min_coverage_views.txt 43.5; no 90% figure remains in README.md or docs/runbooks.

units.key: § 004 — Debt is ratcheted, never waived > Consequence
units.does: Claims .ci numbers are a debt inventory; eighteen waivers went to zero, the last oversized types were split (aggregate_type_size_budget 0, aggregate_type_excess_budget 0), and remaining static composition-root reads are counted in .ci/shared_usage_budget.txt (90). Consistent with .ci contents.
calls: .github/workflows/ci.yml::step lint-and-budgets/Singletons read only in the composition root
